record.provider: SURF Research Drive (Netherlands) — up to 5 TB free via NWO-funded Small Compute applications

free_tier.stated: Community Edition: 'Are you working at an institution without its own Research Drive environment? Then apply for access to Research Drive Community Edition here. You will receive up to 5 TB of storage space.' Institutional instances have their own (much larger) quotas set per institution.

egress.terms: Unmetered. SURF is the Dutch national e-infrastructure, no egress product exists.

record.tooling: Research Drive is ownCloud/Nextcloud-based, so the standard desktop sync client and WebDAV endpoints work; rclone's webdav backend applies. Not S3.
record.chaining: Grants 5 TB per project via Small Compute. The same application also provides up to 10 TB project storage on Snellius, up to 200 TB disk storage and 300 TB tape storage on Grid/Spider for data processing, and up to 50 TB offline tape storage.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: not published for Research Drive; the SURF bundle page caps 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius and 'up to 200TB disk storage' on Grid/Spider. request-rate: not published. Retention: tied to the project; SURF states data is retained for the project duration. Gate: 'researchers must have either a tenured appointment .. or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed'. A genuinely institution-gated, NWO-funded scheme.
record.reliability_note: servicedesk.surf.nl returns 401 to the reader and www.surf.nl intermittently 504s; the numbers here come from the live NWO page and a 2026-03-11 Wayback capture of the Research Drive page.

evidence.proved: 'Research Drive - via SURF max. 5TB or via institution', 'max. 50TB offline tape storage, if required max. 10TB project space storage', 'up to 200TB disk storage, 300TB tape storage', 'tenured appointment ... or a tenure track appointment'

free_tier.stated: A Small Compute application can request "up to and including 1,000,000 CPU or GPU SBU (standard billing units) of cluster computing on Snellius Supercomputer", "Up to and including 500,000 CPU core-hours and/or 14,000 GPU hours of cluster computing on the LUMI pre-exascale supercomputer", "up to and including 1,000,000 CPU core hours or 10,000 GPU hours of Data Processing on Grid and/or Spider", and "up to and including 50,000 CPU core hours or 5,000 GPU hours of cloud computing on HPC Cloud via SURF Research Cloud", with a maximum duration of one year.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: This is the largest set of numbers in the file reachable without a competitive review: 14,000 LUMI GPU-hours plus 500,000 LUMI core-hours plus a million SBU on Snellius, decided on technical feasibility in about two weeks. It composes badly with nothing except the Dutch contract, which is the whole gate.

limits.value: Eligibility is a tenured or tenure-track appointment at a Dutch university, university of applied sciences, university medical centre, KNAW or NWO institute, and a temporary appointment qualifies only if the employer guarantees the project's completion, so the 14,000 LUMI GPU-hours are unreachable without a Dutch contract.
